value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Rialto/San Bernardino County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Main panel size documentation shown on plans
Project scope details: kW DC capacity, module count, battery quantity, inverter count, and solar location

value: Apply through the Online Permitting Center (OPC) using the SolarAPP+ code generated, pay fees, and schedule inspections through the OPC

other_conditions: No building-integrated photovoltaic systems (BIPV) or ballasted systems
Manufactured homes requiring roof-mounted solar must apply separately through California HCD (951-782-4420)
Only C-10 and C-46 licensed contractors may use the SolarAPP+ pathway
Main panel upgrades (MPUs) require a separate permit and cannot proceed through SolarAPP+
Permits can only be issued for one job per property at a time

permit_fees.notes: The page states SolarAPP+ charges its own processing fee and city fees are payable through the OPC, and that the first 3 revisions submitted through SolarAPP+ are free, but no specific dollar figure for the city's own permit fee was stated. Also checked the City's FY23 City Wide Department Fees PDF (yourrialto.com/234/City-Fees) this session, 28 pages; it contains no line item mentioning 'solar' or 'photovoltaic' anywhere.
